implementation_facts.fact: `def add_points(session: Session, learner_id: uuid.UUID, *, points: int, episodes_read: int = 0, words_reviewed: int = 0, questions_correct: int = 0, read_aloud: int = 0, videos_watched: int = 0, day: date | None = None) -> LearningDay`. It does a Postgres `insert(LearningDay).values(id=uuid4(), ..., goal_met=points >= DAILY_GOAL, updated_at=utcnow())` with `.on_conflict_do_update(index_elements=["learner_id","day"], set_={col: LearningDay.col + arg ..., "goal_met": (LearningDay.points + points) >= DAILY_GOAL, "updated_at": utcnow()})`, then re-selects the row with populate_existing. `day` defaults to local_today() (Brussels).

`def streak(session, learner_id, today_date: date | None = None) -> dict`. It loads up to 400 most recent LearningDay rows with points > 0. `current` counts consecutive days from today if today is active, otherwise from yesterday. `best` is the longest consecutive run within those rows. Returns `{"current", "best", "today_active", "today_points", "active_days"}`, where active_days = len(rows), capped at 400.

`def recent_days(session, learner_id, days: int = 14) -> list[dict]` returns 14 entries, oldest first, ending at local_today(): `{"day": iso, "points": int, "goal_met": bool(row and row.points >= DAILY_GOAL)}`.

risks: GET /today requeues automatically after a failure. _unread_episodes excludes 'failed' (stories/service.py:123-127), so every GET /today after a failed episode queues a new episode and job. TodayHome keeps polling while that episode is pending (up to 48 polls, TodayHome.tsx:10-37), so a persistent failure (paid_not_approved, allowance, provider outage, repeated quality failures) can create many failed episodes per page view. Quality failures make up to 2 billed calls per episode, and provider errors charge the estimate. Usage limits are the only cap. It also means the 'failed' card (TodayHome.tsx:85) is rarely visible.

If GET /today stops enqueuing (for example, moved to a POST), about 10 API tests break, because they use GET /today to create the episode (test_stories.py:164-308, the ready_episode helper at 252-255, and the generation tests at 188-247), plus e2e stories.spec.ts:168-176. Docs STORY_ENGINE.md:11 and ENGINEERING.md:333 would also need updating.

GET /today takes `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on story_series twice (ensure_series is called from today_episode and from ensure_buffer, service.py:62,371,183), so concurrent dashboard loads for the same learner serialize.

Changing DAILY_GOAL breaks test_stories.py:168 (goal == {target:20,...}) and the e2e fixture copy 'Nog 20 punten'. Existing learning_days.goal_met values become stale; nothing reads them except test_stories.py:153, since recent_days recomputes.

Day-boundary mismatch: points and streak use Brussels days (today.py:19-20), while usage allowances reset on UTC days (usage/service.py:55-56). Between local midnight and 01:00/02:00 Brussels time the two disagree. Any combined 'today' UI must pick one.

Awarding points from new domains: add_points relies on the Postgres-only `insert ... on_conflict_do_update` (today.py:9,27-43). Import `dlp.domains.stories.today`, not stories.service: stories.service imports curriculum.service (service.py:25), so curriculum importing stories.service would be circular. today.py imports only db.base and stories.models.

A new LearningDay counter needs a model column, a migration 0008 with server_default='0' (as 0007 did for videos_watched), a new add_points kwarg and a new entry in the on_conflict set_. Forgetting the set_ entry silently drops increments on every call after the first in a day.
test_stories.py:344-345 compares plan['words'] to an exact 5-key dict. Adding or removing a key under 'words' (including dropping 'preview') breaks it.

Changing read-aloud to award on the best attempt needs an explicit 'awarded' flag in episode.answers['read_aloud'][key] to avoid double awards. Existing stored entries lack that flag, so their award status cannot be inferred: matched_words is kept as a max, but there is no record of whether points were given.

Word-review points are uncapped: each review with a new request_id gives +1, and an 'again' card is due again after 10 minutes (vocab.py:96,119-123). Any 'review' step logic or goal changes should take into account that points can be farmed.
streak() loads at most 400 active rows (today.py:54-55), so active_days and best are capped and become silently wrong after 400 active days.

GET /export (routes_progress.py:47-115) contains no stories, vocab, videos or learning_days. stories.service.export exists but is not wired to any route. Exposing the LearningDay counters is a new API surface, not a reuse.

Misleading docstrings can mislead implementers: stories/service.py:9 says rating awards points (it does not), videos/service.py:11 says saving words awards points (it does not), and routes_stories.py:1 says 'Reads are free' (GET /today can queue a model job).

TodayHome's 'Lees opnieuw' CTA (TodayHome.tsx:65) is effectively unreachable from /today, because ensure_buffer only returns unread episodes. When unread[0] is queued while unread[1] is ready, next_step is 'wait' even though an episode is ready.

`def objective_result(questions: list[Question], answers: dict[str, int]) -> dict`. Requires set(answers) == the question ids, otherwise 422 'answer each question once; unknown questions are not accepted'. Each value must be a non-bool int in [0, len(options)), otherwise 422. Logic: `correct = sum(answers[q.id] == q.answer_index ...)`, `required = math.ceil(len(questions) * 75 / 100)`, `passed = correct >= required`. Returns {passed,correct,total,required,feedback{nl,en,fa}}. With the usual 2 questions, required is 2 (all correct); with 3 it is 3.

Topic answer keys are returned after any complete submission, pass or fail (topics.py:219-221). Combined with sticky `completed`, a learner can fail once and resubmit the revealed keys. Any 'mastery' metric built on topic practice inherits this.

Pass threshold: ceil(0.75 × 2) = 2, so the usual 2-question activities require all answers correct. risks: Adding fields to ChatResult: tests construct it positionally (test_single_model_call.py:191, test_topic_conversations.py:134,184), so new fields must be appended with defaults. Adding abstract methods to ChatModel breaks FixtureChatModel, the benchmark models in benchmarks/language/harness.py and the test SingleInvocationFixture.

Tests monkeypatch instance methods `complete`/`complete_once` with `(messages, **kwargs)` functions (test_topic_conversations.py:185, test_coaching.py:244, test_curriculum.py:200). A new code path such as `stream()` or `complete_with_tools()` would bypass those patches and silently hit the fixture or a real model.

Tool-call replies: `_first_content` returns "" when message.content is None and drops `tool_calls`. With a schema, that becomes 'schema validation failed' and triggers a repair turn. Tool support therefore needs new parsing, a new ChatMessage shape (roles are Literal system|user|assistant; there is no tool role, tool_call_id or tool_calls field) and new raw fields.

Strict structured output: removing the injected schema system message changes behaviour pinned by tests (test_chat_client.py:43 asserts messages[0] is the schema system message; test_single_model_call.py:114 asserts len(messages)==2). It also changes token-reservation maths that add len(schema_instruction(...)) in topic_conversations/workflow.py:55, coaching:300, content_review:200, stories:256,473 and videos:188. Strict json_schema also needs additionalProperties:false and every property required, which plain pydantic model_json_schema() output with defaults does not satisfy (general OpenAI/Azure rule, not verifiable in the repo).

Azure model compatibility: the body always sends `max_tokens` and `temperature`. Reasoning-family deployments typically require `max_completion_tokens` and reject non-default temperature (general knowledge). The deployed model is an unset deploy parameter (infra/parameters.example.json:14), so it cannot be checked here.

Streaming vs retries: the retry/repair/truncation loop (chat_openai_compatible.py:188-243) cannot be replayed once partial tokens have reached the user. The semaphore would be held for the whole stream. httpx timeout is a single 120 s scalar (registry passes chat_timeout_seconds). Usage then needs stream usage chunks (e.g. stream_options include_usage), otherwise the len//4 estimate path is used.

Usage under-counting already exists: tokens come from the final attempt only; model_calls are committed as 1 per logical call; a swallowed compose_reply failure in practice is charged 0 (workflow.py:112-114 + turns.py:187-188). ProviderUnavailable (connection refused, nothing sent) is charged the full estimate at the commit-estimate sites. Multi-call tool loops need explicit reservation sizing (cf. MODEL_CALLS_PER_TURN=2).

Concurrency: chat and chat_strong are separate instances with separate semaphores, even when both use the same Azure deployment. Semaphore waits block threadpool workers indefinitely. test_concurrent_single_call_does_not_change_legacy_retry_limit uses Barrier(2) and would deadlock/time out if the default max_concurrent dropped below 2.

Proxy for SSE: Last-Event-ID is not forwarded. request.signal is not passed, so a closed tab keeps the upstream (paid) generation running. No buffering-control header is forwarded. next.config.ts leaves `compress` at its default; whether Next compression buffers text/event-stream is unverified. Node fetch (undici) has implicit headers/body timeouts even though no signal is set (general knowledge). apiFetch hard-codes Accept and apiJson consumes JSON.

FastAPI side: `@app.middleware("http")` is a BaseHTTPMiddleware wrapping every response; streaming through it should be tested, including client-disconnect cancellation. Handlers depend on a yield DB session that commits on success (db/session.py:57-60), and the code relies on the transaction committing usage and the failed-turn rows (routes_practice.py:159 'Returned, not raised'). Whether that session is still open while a StreamingResponse body is iterated under fastapi 0.141.1 is unverified; follow the video precedent and keep DB work out of the generator.

LangGraph: graphs are rebuilt and compiled on every call. The topic graph uses recursion_limit=6, which caps any future tool loop. Practice state accumulates model_calls via _record. That list feeds both usage commits and the preflight Azure-evidence SQL (preflight.py:39-44), so changing provider naming (f"azure-{tier}") or the model_calls dict shape can silently flip preflight to integration_pending.

Fixture behaviour: FixtureChatModel ignores temperature/max_tokens and returns no finish_reason or tool calls. Its default replies come from apps/api/tests/fixtures/chat_replies.json (a missing file silently means {} and minimal _example_for objects). A new prompt_version without an entry gets placeholder values ('fixture', 0, False, []), which may fail validators in domain code during e2e runs.

verdicts.claim: 4. AppShell intercepts link clicks (navigation guard) so writing autosave/recording finish before navigation.
verdicts.evidence: AppShell.tsx:71-103: `onClickCapture={navigate}` on div.app-frame (line 108). It acts only when a guard is registered. It ignores modified or non-left clicks, download links, target=_blank, other origins, and same-pathname links. Otherwise it calls preventDefault, awaits guard.current(), and calls router.push only if the guard returns true. Guards are registered through NavigationGuardContext (lib/client/navigation.ts). WritingStep.tsx:76-84 flushes persistRef.current(text) and returns false if the save fails; it reaches the shell through LessonShell.tsx:105-110. CurriculumLesson.tsx:38-45 and CurriculumTest.tsx:26-33 do not wait: while busy or recordingBusy they return false and set the error 'Rond je opname af en wacht tot je werk is bewaard voordat je verdergaat.'
verdicts.correction: The guard only intercepts anchor clicks inside .app-frame, which covers both shell and in-page links. It does not cover browser back/forward, programmatic router.push, or the skip link (layout.tsx:43, outside .app-frame). Mission writing drafts are flushed and then navigation proceeds, or is blocked if the save fails. Curriculum lessons and tests do not wait for recording or saving to finish; they block navigation and show an error. beforeunload is handled only in WritingStep.tsx:69-75. Any new nav built from buttons, a portal outside .app-frame, or router.push would bypass the guard.

verdicts.claim: 5. Every route page.tsx is a thin server component rendering one client component; 41 of 42 components are "use client"; there are no loading.tsx files.

Most of the 13 page.tsx files render a single component, but missions/page.tsx:6 renders an inline <header> plus MissionCatalog. progress/page.tsx:6 renders CurriculumProgress plus <details><summary>Voortgang in praktijkgesprekken</summary><ProgressOverview nested/></details>. settings/page.tsx:7-34 renders a header plus AccountSettings, StatusPanel and UsagePanel. speech-check/page.tsx renders a header, an aside callout and SpeechCheck. app/error.tsx is "use client"; app/not-found.tsx is a server component.

Pages are server components, but four of them (missions, progress, settings, speech-check) compose server-rendered headings with several client components, and those headings are pinned by e2e. No pages have metadata titles for speech-check, missions/[missionId], learn/[stageId] or learn/[stageId]/test. layout.tsx sets `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` (line 37).

verdicts.claim: 6. The first-visit Today screen shows a "writer is busy" waiting card polling every 5s (TodayHome.tsx) and zero-valued streak stats.

implementation_facts.topic: How unit tests, lint and typecheck run
implementation_facts.fact: apps/web/package.json scripts: "test:unit": "node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/unit/*.test.mjs" (files: alphabet, audio-focus, draft-saver, microphone-request, phrase-audio, sentences; none touch the shell or nav); "test:e2e": "playwright test"; "lint": "eslint ."; "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"; "build": "next build". Requires Node >=22.6.0 and @playwright/test 1.56.0. The API test that pins Today is apps/api/tests/test_stories.py::test_today_queues_an_episode_and_the_job_writes_a_validated_one.

risks: The mobile bottom bar has its column count hard-coded to six (design.css:1333 `repeat(6, minmax(0, 1fr))`). Changing the number of mobile:true links without updating it breaks the layout. The 390/320px overflow checks and axe checks in design.spec run on every main screen.

The navigation guard only sees same-origin <a href> clicks bubbling through div.app-frame (AppShell.tsx:71-108). A regrouped nav that uses buttons, router.push, or a menu or drawer rendered in a portal outside .app-frame would skip the draft flush. That loses mission drafts and fails design.spec 'primary navigation waits for a writing draft to be saved'.

Accessible names are load-bearing. 'Hoofdmenu' + link 'Mijn voortgang' (design.spec:95-105), 'Hoofdmenu' + link 'Praktijkgesprekken' (resilience.spec:11), and 'Mobiel hoofdmenu' + link "Video's" (videos.spec:155) must keep working, or those specs must be updated. If Praktijkgesprekken moves into a submenu, the link may become hidden and the click fails.

The Today h1 regex in design.spec.ts:8 (/aflevering|woorden wachten|Kies waar je vandaag mee begint/) and stories.spec exact strings ('Er ligt een nieuwe aflevering klaar.', 'Je volgende aflevering wordt geschreven.', 'De schrijver is bezig…', '4 dagen op rij', 'Nog 20 punten tot je dagdoel.', 'Wie is wie in De Lindestraat', link 'Mijn leerpad Twaalf niveaus met woorden, grammatica en toetsen.' → /leerpad, /3 woorden om te herhalen/ → /woorden, testids today-home and episode-card) all pin the current Today design. A redesign must update them together. Removing the streak ring role=img breaks design.spec:48.

The LanguageSwitcher label 'Taalhulp / language' is used as a selector in about 15 places across 8 specs, on /learn/*, /verhalen/* and mission pages, including at 320px. Moving the switcher into settings or a collapsed menu, or renaming the label, breaks many unrelated specs.

GET /today has a side effect: ensure_buffer queues a model call. A Today redesign that stops calling /today, or changes the queue-on-read behaviour, breaks the API test test_today_queues_an_episode_and_the_job_writes_a_validated_one and e2e 'the real API queues the first episode for a new learner'. Because JOB_LOOP_ENABLED=false in e2e, the unmocked Today page always sits in the 'wait' state.

Hiding raw failure_reasons (<code>) conflicts with stories.spec.ts:90-91 and videos.spec.ts:89-90, which assert 'sentence_too_long: … (limit 12)' is visible after clicking 'Wat er niet klopte'. Changing the ConnectionBanner copy is safe (resilience.spec checks only the testid, data-state and the 'Opnieuw proberen' button).

Changing register (u → je) must skip target-language content. CommunicationCoach phrases ('Kunt u dat herhalen?', asserted in learning-tools.spec.ts:38) and the character turns in conversation fixtures (conversation.spec.ts:58 'Uw nieuwe afspraak…', learning-agents.spec 'Wat wilt u kopen?') are practice Dutch.

Several page headings live in server page.tsx files, not components ('Jouw leeromgeving.' in settings, 'Jouw stem. Jouw Nederlands.' in speech-check, 'Uw oefenbibliotheek' in missions), and the progress page wraps ProgressOverview in a details element whose summary text 'Voortgang in praktijkgesprekken' is clicked by catalog.spec:50. Merging or moving pages must keep these, or update the tests. ProgressOverview without `nested` renders a second h1 'Elke stap vertelt iets.', which duplicates CurriculumProgress's h1.

sectionFor() and the `?? links[0]` fallback determine aria-current and the breadcrumb. Regrouping routes (e.g. /woorden or /videos under a new parent) needs sectionFor updated, or the wrong tab is marked current and the breadcrumb wrongly shows 'Vandaag'.

Below 768px, .profile-button is hidden (learning.css:220) and settings is not in the bottom bar, so phone users have no shell route to Instellingen. Settings also hosts the usage, budget and technical panels.

Interface language: <html lang="nl"> is fixed, and LanguageProvider's server snapshot is 'nl-en'. Adding UI-language switching (English/Persian chrome) has no i18n infrastructure to build on and would cause hydration flips. Persian chrome would also need dir=rtl at a higher level. Most specs assert Dutch literals.

Playwright has no webServer. Local runs need `python scripts/run.py e2e` (Postgres test DB ending in _test, Python venv, npm build), and only lesson/steps specs run in the tablet and phone-width projects. Shell regressions at mobile widths are caught only where specs call setViewportSize (design, videos, catalog, curriculum, skill-topics, zz-reliability).

verdicts.claim: 1. coaching/service.py candidate_plan is pure deterministic code returning exactly 3 items; the only model involvement is an optional reorder (_rank_once, complete_once) validated by validate_ranking; plans are cached by history version.
verdicts.evidence: candidate_plan (domains/coaching/service.py:160-221) has no I/O. It builds items with add() and the skill loop stops at `if len(items) == 3: break` (:208-209). Test test_fresh_plan_has_three_real_localized_activities_without_claiming_weakness asserts 3 unique ids. The only model call is _rank_once -> providers.chat.complete_once(..., schema=PlanRanking, max_output_tokens=600, temperature=0.0, prompt_version=POLICY_VERSION) (:311), checked by validate_ranking (:235-243). Cache: get_plan (:224-232) and personalise_plan (:271-276) look up CoachPlanRequest by (learner_id, stage_id, history_version, policy_version). Only personalise_plan inserts a row (:282-285).
verdicts.correction: The core claim holds, with these corrections. (a) candidate_plan returns a tuple (plan, evidence), not just a plan. Three items are guaranteed only because TopicBank has min_length=100 topics and there are 4 SKILLS. (b) Only POST /coach/plan writes the cache. GET never writes and returns the uncached deterministic plan until some POST has happened. (c) A POST with an already-used request_id returns the stored response no matter what the history is now (:262-267). (d) Fallback plans are cached too, including fixture mode, Azure without paid_usage_enabled, provider outage and usage limit (:278-285). After one transient failure, further POSTs for the same history_version return the cached 'fallback' and never retry the model. (e) The model is skipped completely when can_personalise is False, i.e. when there is no current history.

verdicts.claim: 5. Mission role-play (practice/workflow.py) runs propose_action (model) → apply_action (code) → compose_reply (model, anchored on a fixed line, with a contradiction guard that falls back to the fixed line); service scenarios use fixed lines only.
verdicts.evidence: workflow.py:58-131: the graph is propose_action -> validate_action (apply_action) -> compose_reply. Service branch: :89-99 returns reply_source 'fixed_line'. Guard: :119-120 `if not reply or _contradicts_decision(...): return {"reply_nl": anchor or reply, ...}`. On ProviderError: :112-114 `anchor or "Sorry, kunt u dat herhalen?"`. Exactly one model call per service turn (test_service_missions.py:132-141 asserts len(chat.calls) == 1). implementation_facts.fact: POLICY_VERSION = "practice-plan-v1"; HISTORY_WINDOW = 100. Signatures: `def candidate_plan(bank: topics.TopicBank, history: list[PracticeObservation], count: int) -> tuple[dict, dict]` (plan, evidence {item_id: [obs_id,..<=2]}); `def get_plan(session, learner_id: uuid.UUID, stage_id: str) -> dict`; `def personalise_plan(session, settings, providers, *, learner_id, stage_id, request_id) -> dict`; `def validate_ranking(reply: PlanRanking, plan: dict, evidence) -> list[dict]`; `def _rank_once(session, settings, providers, learner_id, plan, evidence, request_id) -> dict`. history_version = fingerprint({count, episodes: [ids of <=100 rows], content: sha256(bank json)}). basis values: recent_attempt | repeated_attempts | transfer | unpractised_skill | start. mode values: suggested | personalised | fallback.

`def history_page(session, learner_id, stage_id: str, limit: int = 20, offset: int = 0) -> dict` returns {"stage_id","offset","limit","items":[observation_view]}, 404 for unknown stage, 422 unless 1<=limit<=50. `def record_observation(session, *, learner_id, stage_id, topic_id, skill: Skill, source: str, request_id: str, content_version: str, passed: bool | None, summary: dict, failed_refs: list[str], payload: dict, response: dict | None = None) -> PracticeObservation`. It requires topic_id.startswith(f"{stage_id}-t"), 1<=len(request_id)<=80 and source in (topic_practice, conversation), and truncates failed_refs to 12. observation_view keys: id, stage_id, topic_id, skill, source, content_version, passed, summary, failed_refs, created_at (payload_hash and response are never exposed). Also: `export_observations(session, learner_id) -> list[dict]` and `paid_model_guard(session, learner_id)` (advisory xact lock 'paid-model:{id}' that raises 409).

Table practice_observations: id UUID pk; learner_id FK learners.id ON DELETE CASCADE; stage_id String(20); topic_id String(60); skill String(20); source String(30); request_id String(80); payload_hash String(64); content_version String(64); passed Boolean nullable; summary JSONB; failed_refs JSONB list; response JSONB (replay only); created_at timestamptz. UniqueConstraint(learner_id, source, request_id); Index(learner_id, stage_id, created_at). Table coach_plan_requests: id, learner_id (CASCADE), stage_id(20), request_id(80), history_version(64), policy_version(40), response JSONB, created_at; UniqueConstraint(learner_id, request_id); Index(learner_id, stage_id, history_version, policy_version). Migration: apps/api/migrations/versions/0005_learning_support.py. summary shapes: receptive topic_practice {correct,total,assessed:true}; productive {word_count,criteria_met,criteria_total,assessed}; conversation {assessed,assisted,goals_met,goals_total,input_mode,topic_content_version}.

Router prefix /coach. `GET /coach/plan?stage_id=` -> service.get_plan (no writes, no model). `POST /coach/plan` with body PlanBody {"stage_id": str(2-20), "request_id": str(8-80, ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$)}, extra=forbid -> personalise_plan. `GET /coach/history?stage_id=&limit=20(1-50)&offset=0(0-100000)` -> history_page. Plan JSON: {"stage_id":"a2","history_version":"<64 hex>","history_count":1,"mode":"suggested","can_personalise":true,"items":[{"id":"a2-t001:reading","stage_id":"a2","topic_id":"a2-t001","skill":"reading","title":{nl,en,fa},"category":{nl,en,fa},"reason":{nl,en,fa},"basis":"recent_attempt","evidence_count":1}, ...3 items],"notice":{nl,en,fa}}. @contextmanager
def session_scope() -> Iterator[Session]:
    session = _factory()()

risks: Moving provider calls outside the row lock in content_review, stories or videos changes behaviour that tests pin. test_expired_job_lease_cannot_cause_concurrent_provider_calls expects the second worker to block on FOR UPDATE and then see 'needs_review'. Without the lock it would see 'running' and mark the review failed/'interrupted'. Any refactor needs a different at-most-once guard, such as a claim token or generation compare-and-swap.

Lease expiry during a long handler: if a second worker (a CLI run-jobs, an overlapping revision or a scale-out) reclaims an expired 60 s lease, its handler blocks on the domain row's FOR UPDATE. statement_timeout=30000 then raises OperationalError, which run_job records as a retry or dead. If it instead gets the lock in the brief window between a handler's mid-run commit and its re-lock (stories/service.py:269-270, videos _reload), it sees 'generating' or 'writing' and marks a healthy in-flight episode or video failed/'interrupted'. The first worker then returns 'obsolete'.

Usage counter row locks: request-scoped flows (practice turns, feedback, curriculum, topic practice, speech) take usage_counters row locks in reserve and hold them across provider calls until the request commits. A second paid request from the same learner blocks for up to 30 s and then fails with QueryCanceled (sqlstate 57014). That is not handled by any _run (only 55P03 is), so it surfaces as a 500 'internal error'.

Connection pool: 5+5 connections per process with a 10 s pool_timeout. Each long locked request holds a connection, and the job loop uses one. Sync endpoints run in AnyIO's default 40-thread pool, so concurrency above about 9 long calls will hit pool timeouts.

The commit-on-return contract is implicit. Changing a `return JSONResponse(...)` to `raise HTTPException(...)` (or the reverse) in routes_practice (_failed_turn_response, _speech_error) or any _run silently changes whether the failed turn, released or committed usage, and STT audio usage persist. test_turns.py:190 and test_speech_recovery.py:150 pin this. A unified exception handler must not move these paths onto the rollback path.

FastAPI 0.141.1 and Starlette 1.6.0 are locked. Before relying on 'commit before response', verify whether yield-dependency teardown (the commit) runs before or after the response is sent. If it runs after, commit failures are invisible to clients and a client may read before the write commits.

Unknown-kind poison job: a KeyError at jobs/service.py:118 sits outside the try, so the job is never dead-lettered. claim_next does not check max_attempts and orders by run_after, so the poison job is re-claimed first on every run after lease expiry and blocks the CLI drain. Fix both the registration (a shared 'register all handlers' import used by main.py and cli.py) and the guard (move the lookup inside the try, or mark the job dead).

Story retry idempotency-key collision: stories/service.py:457 keys retries by `episode.attempts`. If a retried episode fails again before attempts increments (allowance or paid_not_approved paths, or 'interrupted'), the next retry reuses the key. enqueue returns the old done job, and the episode stays 'queued' forever with no job. Videos avoid this by adding a timestamp (:547).

SceneCardRenderer.start renders synchronously inside the video_script job (TTS per scene plus several ffmpeg runs, each up to ffmpeg_timeout*9 = 180 s), and poll_render runs media.finalize (up to 120 s) and blob.put. Both routinely exceed the 60 s lease. The single-threaded JobLoop also delays every other job kind meanwhile.

Changing the error mappers changes the API contract that the web client depends on. Practice, speech and missions return 502 for ProviderError and 503 for ProviderUnavailable, with 'speech-to-text failed: ...' style details. _run users return 503 with a fixed message. 429 bodies differ: str(UsageLimitExceeded) vs a fixed message. The practice 502 body carries extra 'turn' and 'session' keys. Tests assert substrings of detail (e.g. 'model endpoint unreachable', 'injected fixture failure').

Adding response_model would filter and validate outputs. Many views return ad-hoc dicts with optional keys (episode_view adds keys only when status=='ready', turn_view, _session_view), and some routes return Response or StreamingResponse objects. Strict models could drop fields or 500 on drift, and enabling openapi in non-development changes the attack surface the docs deliberately avoid.

The unhandled-exception handler is registered for Exception, so it runs in ServerErrorMiddleware outside the http middleware. call_next raises, so request_metadata skips its header block: unhandled 500s lack the X-Request-Id, X-Response-Time-Ms, Cache-Control and nosniff headers from the API (the web proxy re-adds x-request-id).

Telemetry export is limited to the 'dlp.telemetry' logger (unused). Adding trace propagation means forwarding `traceparent` in FORWARDED_REQUEST_HEADERS (route.ts:19) and extracting context in request_span. Adding structured logs must respect observability.py's rule against exporting bodies, prompts, headers, full URLs or user identifiers.

In settings, job_max_attempts=5 is never read. Wiring it into enqueue's default would not change production behaviour, because every real call site passes max_attempts. Changing the Job model or DB default needs an Alembic migration (0001 created the table).

implementation_facts.fact: apiFetch builds `/api/${path.replace(/^\/+/, "")}` and sends headers {"X-Requested-With": "fetch", "X-Request-Id": options.requestId ?? newRequestId(), Accept: "application/json, audio/wav"}. With a body (and no formData) it adds Content-Type: application/json and JSON.stringify(body); formData is sent as is. It always uses cache: "no-store" and credentials: "same-origin". On a network error it dispatches CustomEvent("dlp:connectivity", {detail: {reachable: false}}) unless the error is an AbortError DOMException, then rethrows. After any response it dispatches reachable = (status !== 502). apiJson reads x-request-id, tries response.json() (payload stays null on parse failure) and, if !response.ok, throws new ApiError(status, payload.detail ? String(payload.detail) : response.statusText, requestId). On success it returns `payload as T`, so a 204 or empty body returns null (words.remove is typed apiJson<null>). There is no retry, timeout or 401 redirect.

implementation_facts.topic: Same-origin proxy contract any client must respect
implementation_facts.fact: app/api/[...path]/route.ts exports GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE, all through handle(). For POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE it returns 403 {detail: "request refused: missing X-Requested-With header"} unless x-requested-with is "fetch"; it also checks sec-fetch-site and Origin. X-Request-Id must match /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{8,64}$/ or it is replaced. Bodies over 6 MB return 413. An unreachable upstream returns 502 {detail: "the API is not reachable", request_id}. Forwarded response headers include x-request-id and x-audio-voice. Video media and subtitle URLs are used directly as `/api/${video.media_url}` (VideoPlayer.tsx:74-75).

risks: Any new data layer (SWR, react-query or a custom hook) must keep going through apiFetch. ConnectionBanner depends on its dlp:connectivity events, which resilience.spec.ts pins, and the proxy refuses unsafe methods without X-Requested-With: fetch (route.ts:48).

Unit tests can only import modules with no imports, no path aliases and no non-erasable TypeScript. Node --experimental-strip-types cannot resolve "@/..." or extensionless "./api", and api.ts's ApiError uses constructor parameter properties (`public readonly status`), which strip-types rejects. Testing api.ts or the stories/videos clients therefore needs a refactor or a different runner. The script globs only tests/unit/*.test.mjs, so a new *.test.ts file would silently not run.

Because tests/ is excluded from tsconfig, type changes to shared API types (TodayPlan, Video and so on) will not break e2e fixtures at compile time. Stale route fixtures in stories.spec.ts and videos.spec.ts can drift silently.

E2E route mocks match exact URL shapes (/\/api\/today(?:\?|$)/, /\/api\/videos(?:\?|$)/, /\/api\/curriculum$/). Adding query parameters, renaming paths or prefetching would break interception. content-review.spec.ts also asserts that /settings makes no /content-review/ request for non-admins, so a shared prefetch must not trigger one.

Pollers drive load() through state (setPolls) and are throttled by POLL_LIMIT (48 for TodayHome, 150 for VideoLibrary). ContentReviewQueue polls forever while items are queued or running. Replacing them with refetchInterval changes stall semantics and the "Het duurt langer dan verwacht" UI.

ApiError.detail is String(payload.detail). For FastAPI 422 validation errors detail is an array, so it becomes "[object Object]". Several components show cause.detail on 409 or as a fallback (TodayHome:42, EpisodeReader/VideoPlayer friendly, VideoLibrary:82, StoryLibrary, WordReview:43), and the API's 409 strings are English, so English text appears in the Dutch UI.

Unifying the multiple-choice components is risky: CurriculumQuestions judges locally from answer_index and uses radio name q-{id}; QuestionList awaits a server verdict per question in sequence and has e2e test ids (result-*, earlier-*, *-check, score, *-done); Episode/Video Questions send one POST with a stable requestId (idempotency) and plain-string options. In exam mode CurriculumQuestions must show Dutch only, with no PhraseAudio.

Merging the two countWords implementations changes the min/max word gating (WritingStep vs CurriculumRecorder/CurriculumTest/SkillTopicPractice) and may break steps.spec or curriculum.spec expectations.

Fixing sign-out clearing by widening the prefix match to all 'taalstudio.' keys would also wipe the language preference (taalstudio.language-support), which curriculum.spec "support languages ... persist after reload" and learning-agents.spec (sets it via addInitScript) rely on. Sign-out is an <a href="/.auth/logout"> link with onClick, so clearing must stay synchronous.

Replacing hard-coded 'De Lindestraat' in EpisodeReader needs an API change (episode_view has no series fields) or an extra stories.library/today fetch. EpisodeCard is shared with StoryLibrary, and the e2e tests assert the literal 'Wie is wie in De Lindestraat' (from series.title) and the story-library h1.
Passing mission.cefr_target to WritingCoach needs lower-casing ("A2" to "a2"), because the route is curriculum/{stage}/writing-feedback with lower-case stage ids.

Keyed-result state (result.key === key) is what prevents stale responses from rendering, and library-writing.spec "delayed word searches never pair an updated pager with stale cards" pins it. A refactor that drops the key check or the AbortController reintroduces races.

I could not verify whether the react-hooks/set-state-in-effect rule is actually active because node_modules is absent. Run `npm run lint` after refactors, since a new hook that calls setState synchronously in an effect may fail CI (ci.yml:108-110).
